extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, and researchers interested in BBC projects, public-sector IT programme management, and broadcast-technology history
extracted.subtask_short: documenting a failed BBC IT project
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic summary of the BBC's Digital Media Initiative (DMI), describing aims, timeline, contractors, criticisms, investigations, and outcomes. The page is targeted to readers seeking a factual account of the project's development and failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, achievable project objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme aimed to streamline broadcast operations by moving to a fully digital, tapeless production workflow and to provide features such as media ingest, media asset management, online storyboarding, and metadata storage and sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project goals should be specific and technically feasible (e.g., 'tapeless production workflow', 'unifying audio, video and stills archival'). The article cites DMI's stated features (media ingest system, media asset management, storyboarding, metadata storage) as the intended deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credible business case and realistic cost/benefit forecasts
rubrics_metrics.description: DMI was forecast to deliver cost savings of around £18 million while costing £81.7 million (later reported spend was much higher); costs rose after technical problems and delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business-case assumptions must be realistic and continuously validated; the DMI example shows that optimistic forecasts and escalated costs (final reported spend ~£98m between 2010–2012) can lead to project cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust procurement and tendering processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Siemens was selected to run the project allegedly 'without a tendering process' because of an existing 10-year support contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sole-source selection without competition; the NAO criticised selection without tendering, implying proper procurement safeguards are required to ensure value and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate contract design and risk allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer of risk to Siemens resulted in a 'distant relationship' that made monitoring milestones and deliverables difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts must allocate risk but preserve sufficient managerial levers and transparency for the commissioning organisation; transferring risk should not create inability to verify progress or obtain deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective monitoring of milestones and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC managers reported difficulties in monitoring project milestones and the completion of deliverables; on enquiry they found 'the project was not going according to plan at all' and asked, 'Where are these deliverables? Where is the software?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programme management should include verifiable milestones, evidence of software/deliverables, and regular progress checks; lack of demonstrable deliverables is a red flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined deliverables with demonstrable evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked to show deliverables/software, BBC staff could not find them, indicating a lack of tangible outputs corresponding to contract claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliverables must be unambiguously defined in contracts and accompanied by demonstrable artefacts (software, documentation, etc.); absence of such evidence undermines project credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance, leadership accountability and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior executives were suspended or had contracts terminated (e.g., John Linwood suspended and later had his contract terminated) and the project was described by governance bodies as a 'complete failure'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear governance structures, accountability mechanisms, and escalation paths are required so that leadership is held to account and corrective action can be taken when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accurate reporting to oversight bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: The NAO criticised the BBC's handling of the project and there were claims that Parliament/auditors had been misled about progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations must provide truthful, timely information to auditors, trustees and parliamentary/oversight bodies; misleading reporting damages trust and invites formal inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to submit to external audit and investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The NAO commenced an inquiry and PwC were commissioned to investigate the failure; the House of Commons Public Accounts Committee heard evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large public projects should be amenable to external scrutiny; independent reviews (NAO, PwC) are appropriate responses to serious governance or delivery concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency and capacity for legacy-content migration
rubrics_metrics.description: During Thatcher coverage in 2013, staff were unable to transfer analog videotape from the BBC Archives to digital format due to limited transfer facilities, with tapes being transported by taxi and Tube and external companies used for transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes that migrate legacy media must ensure sufficient technical capacity and contingency plans for demand spikes during major news events; failure to plan for legacy conversion can disrupt operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure readiness and facilities planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports suggested tape editing equipment might have to be installed in specially cooled areas at Broadcasting House.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical infrastructure and environmental controls must be planned and provisioned in advance when projects require specialised equipment or handling of legacy media; retrofitting indicates poor planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff welfare and resourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC staff who worked on DMI and other projects suffered severe stress and were treated at The Priory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programme delivery plans should address workload, staffing levels, and employee wellbeing; chronic overwork or stress among staff is an operational and reputational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial controls, escalation and settlement handling
rubrics_metrics.description: After technical problems and contract termination, BBC losses were estimated at £38.2m, partially offset by a £27.5m settlement with Siemens, leaving a £10.7m loss; costs rose after problems and delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong financial controls and early escalation of cost overruns are necessary. Contract termination and settlements should be managed to minimise public loss; poor controls can produce large unplanned spend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding conflicts from automatic vendor selection based on existing contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Siemens' selection was linked to a pre-existing 10-year support contract, which was cited as the reason for bypassing tendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing vendor relationships should not automatically preclude open competition; governance should manage conflicts of interest and ensure procurement delivers best value.
